title: Composition of qcqs etale compact-support candidates
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. All derived categories below are the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper, set $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and choose compactifications $c_f,c_g,c_{gf}$ of these three morphisms. Then there is a natural isomorphism $Rg_!^{c_g}Rf_!^{c_f}\cong R(gf)_!^{c_{gf}}$ on $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition; finite-ring bounded-below specialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] to the chosen compactification $c_g=(i,\overline g)$. Obtain $e=(a,p)$, $U$, $b$, $p_Y$ and $c$ as in its statement. Write $d_f=(c,p_Y)$ and $d_{gf}=(a,\overline g\circ p)$. These are actual compactifications; in particular $c,b$ are quasi-compact open immersions, $p,p_Y$ are proper, $a=b\circ c$, and $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$. These are exactly the geometric models in the first paragraph of 0F7J, without assuming the original three chosen compactifications form a Cartesian triangle.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, label lemma-shriek-composition, first paragraph and four-line calculation

proof.text: For the successive opens $X\xrightarrow{c}U\xrightarrow{b}\overline X$, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies maps $b_!c_!F\to H$ successively with maps $c_!F\to b^{-1}H$, then with maps $F\to c^{-1}b^{-1}H$. Open inverse image is restriction: evaluation on objects over $X$ gives $c^{-1}b^{-1}H=a^{-1}H$ since $a=bc$; the same cited adjunction identifies the last maps with maps $a_!F\to H$. Thus uniqueness of a left adjoint supplies $b_!c_!\cong a_!$, naturally in $F$. All these Hom bijections are $\Lambda$-linear. The exactness and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] allow this isomorphism to be applied degreewise and then localized, giving $b_!c_!\cong a_!$ on $D^+$. This is the open case of Tag 0F50, with its argument written here rather than creating a node.

The defining square for $U$ satisfies [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-proper-interchange], with proper vertical map $p$ and quasi-compact open horizontal map $i$. Applying its natural isomorphism to $c_!K$ gives $i_!Rp_{Y,*}c_!K\cong Rp_*b_!c_!K$ for every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Degreewise exact extension by zero keeps $c_!K$ bounded below. Finite $\Lambda$ is a torsion ring (some positive integer annihilates its additive group), so no invertibility hypothesis on a prime or on residue characteristics is needed.

For fixed coefficients, the source library already proves the bounded-below composition API. The exact left adjoint upperStar in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] makes lowerStar preserve injective objects by Mathlib's Functor.preservesInjectiveObjects_of_adjunction_of_preservesMonomorphisms. Apply the proved source theorem Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompIso' directly to the underived lowerStarComp comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. This gives Rp_* followed by R(gbar)_* isomorphic to R(p followed by gbar)_* on the same bounded-below module-sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus no ringed-topos presentation, K-injective comparison, or restriction of an unbounded functor is needed. Using [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], write the compatible models as c_! followed by RpY_* and a_! followed by R(p followed by gbar)_*. Associate the four factors, whisker the step-3 interchange on both sides, associate again, whisker the step-2 comparison c_! followed by b_! isomorphic to a_!, and whisker the bounded-below direct-image composition comparison. This yields an isomorphism from the composite of the two compatible model functors to the model functor for f followed by g.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, first, second and fourth equalities; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E, label lemma-derived-pushforward-composition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence] for $f$ and $gf$, whose sources and bases are the original qcqs schemes and whose morphisms are separated of finite type. Its comparisons give $Rf_!^{c_f}\cong Rf_!^{d_f}$ and $R(gf)_!^{d_{gf}}\cong R(gf)_!^{c_{gf}}$. Whisker the first with $Rg_!^{c_g}$, compose with the isomorphism of step 4, and then compose with the second comparison. The result is the required natural isomorphism $Rg_!^{c_g}Rf_!^{c_f}\cong R(gf)_!^{c_{gf}}$. The statement asks for existence of a natural isomorphism for the specified choices; it does not assert unit, associativity or independence of the auxiliary triangle for this composition map. Those stronger coherence assertions of 0F7J are consequently unnecessary here.
